title: Deterministic Zeckendorf games: Split Smallest exactly, Combine Smallest's constant
statement: In the deterministic Zeckendorf games of Li, Li, Miller et al., every play has n - Z(n) merging moves and length sum_{i in Zeck(n)} c_i - sum over add-consecutive moves of (j - 2). For Split Smallest the length is exactly n - Z(n) + sum_{w in L, w < w*} tr1(w) + E(w*, n - val(w*)): while two 1's remain, SS runs the lazy Fibonacci counter through the language L of binary words with no 00 except one final 00 followed only by 1's, in increasing order, making tr1 (trailing ones of the previous word) splits per step; it stops at the first word w* of value >= n - 1, which is lazy; and the end phase makes E = sum over blocks of 1's of floor((k - 1 + g)^2/4) splits with a carry g. The split count is Fibonacci-regular: a 9-dimensional representation over the Zeckendorf blocks 0 and 10 is exact for all n (computer-assisted proof: (w*, a) is the lazy representation of n, the formula is a rational series in it, a 9-state transducer relates Zeckendorf and lazy words, and the composed representation is decided equal to the 9-dimensional one). Consequently the block law holds, and with G_k = F_{k+1} (G_0 = 1, G_1 = 2), S_SS(G_k) = S_SS(G_k - 1) = G_{k+1} - (2k^2 + 8k + 15 + (-1)^k)/8 for all k. Combine Smallest shows full Hankel rank in the tested window. Combine Smallest has length c n + O(log^2 n) with c = 1/2 + sum_{j>=1} (1/F_{2j})(1 - 1/F_{2j+2}) = sum_{k>=1} 1/f_{2k-1} - 1/phi = 1.2064811686570297..., f the standard Fibonacci numbers; c is transcendental. The proof: CS lifts a pile two indices at a time, and the counter below the pile, fed one piece per split, runs a self-similar cycle in which F_{s+1} feeds cost exactly F_{s+1} - 1 moves. Consequently L_SS(n) = phi^2 n - O(log^2 n), both directions of the Split Smallest part of Li et al.'s Conjecture 1.4.
resolves: Li, Li, Miller et al. (2020) open question 'how long do the deterministic games take and who wins as a function of n' for Split Smallest, by an exact formula with written proof; and Li et al. Conjecture 1.4 for Combine Smallest (length linear in n, constant about 1.206), with the constant identified in closed form, by written proof
verified: For every n <= 3000 and all four deterministic games: n - Z(n) merging moves and the length identity hold, CL and SL have length n - Z(n), and SS equals the maximum game length computed over the full game graph for n <= 40.

The SS linear representation reproduces the SS split count for every n <= 120,000 (C simulator output, SHA-256 recorded), the Fibonacci closed form holds for every F_k <= 120,000, and the block law has no violation; perturbing one representation entry breaks agreement.
Hankel ranks over Zeckendorf words: SS 6, 6, 6 and CS 13, 21, 34 at word lengths 6, 7, 8; the CS length ratio is 1.206480 at n = 9,227,465.

Counter lemma (written proof, gated for 20,000 steps): while two 1's remain, each SS step moves the upper word to the radix-order successor in the language of binary words with no 00 except one final 00 followed only by 1's (the lazy Fibonacci representations plus a transient tail), making as many splits as the previous word has trailing 1's.

End-phase lemma (written proof) checked on every lazy word of length <= 14 with 0 or 1 leftover ones; the assembled exact formula matches simulation for every n <= 3000 in the bundled gates and every n <= 120,000 in the recorded large-range check.

Independent review (fresh agent, own simulator): exact formula matches for n <= 3000; E matches SS on all 8,360 lazy states of length <= 16; the proof is correct up to a too-weak run-lemma hypothesis and a misstated r = 0 case, both fixed in 0.3.0.

Combine Smallest (cs_constant.py, n <= 3000): the counter's one-feed rule matches direct simulation for every normal state, s <= 14; the counter cycle for s <= 18; the pile cycle for i <= 10; every tail case for even P <= 14; the level form at every level start; the three forms of c agree to 45 digits; a mutated counter model fails. The C simulators give L_CS(n) - c n in [-16.41, -1.21] for n <= 30,000 and between -22 and -5 at n = 10^3, ..., 10^9 and 4 x 10^9.

Second independent review (fresh agent, own simulators): the Combine Smallest proof is correct up to wording fixes, now applied; one-feed lemma for s <= 16, round and tail lemmas in place for even P <= 18, level form to n <= 30,000 and samples to 10^9, budget lemma on 3,000 random configurations. The exact polylog algorithm cs_exact.py, built only from the lemmas, matches direct simulation for every n <= 30,000 and the C simulator at n up to 4 x 10^9.

SS regularity (ss_regularity.py): component automata W, T, E' replayed exhaustively against their definitions; the counter's stop equals lazy(n) for n < 2000; Rel sound on all aligned pairs of length <= 10 and complete by subset construction, stable under a larger bound; the composed 252-dimensional representation matches the game for n <= 600 and is exactly equivalent to the 9-dimensional one (reachable space of dimension 36); block law and closed forms decided; perturbing the 9-dimensional representation breaks equivalence.

Third independent review (fresh agent): SS regularity proof correct given the §4 lemmas; independent simulator confirms the stop equals lazy(n) for n <= 4000; T, E', S_lazy on 300 random words up to length 80; Rel on random n up to 10^30; opposite-direction equivalence (dimension 42). Wording fixes applied.
unresolved: a proof-assistant version of the written proofs (SS counting and end-phase lemmas, CS counter lemma)
an exact description of Combine Smallest lengths, and a proof that they are not Fibonacci-regular
a proof that L_CS(n) - c n is Theta(log n) (observed: about -0.42 log_phi n); a closed form for the CS winner
nonclaims: the length identity is a rewriting of Cusenza et al.'s exact move-count formula, not a new result
CS non-regularity is evidenced by Hankel rank growth, not proved
the CS error term is O(log^2 n) by written proof; the observed growth -0.42 log_phi n is not proved
the SS regularity proof is computer-assisted on top of the written exact formula; the parity automaton's size is not computed
smallest_decisive_test: An n where the SS split count differs from the 9-dimensional representation, or a counter-language step that does not follow the counting-phase lemma; for CS, a counter state where one feed does not follow the A/B/C rule.
